subject: Medicore VPC commercial model and SLA tempo
messages:
From: Jane Park <jane.park@medicore.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@medicore.com
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Medicore VPC: initial ask + budget guardrails

Hi Soojin / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached is a short RFP with our expected usage profile and a few procurement guardrails (see Medicore_RFP_Q3.pdf). High level asks:

- We need a commercial construct for an on-prem/VPC deployment that separates the perpetual license (per-site) from the annual platform fee.
- We need optionality on an SRE/on-call retainer vs. per-incident pricing.
- Medicore wants a staged discount tied to pilot → production conversion (pilot running 30 days; conversion decision inside 60 days).
- Critical: response windows during the pilot can be laxer, but production SLAs need to be tighter; we're asking for an early-stage credit if we hit conversion milestones.

Budget signal: we can commit to a 12‑month minimum but prefer the first 90 days to be priced as a pilot (reduced platform fee). Can you send a single-slide commercial summary and an indication of the kinds of credits you can offer for pilot->prod conversion?

Also please include any legal/escrow asks up front so our procurement team can review simultaneously.

Thanks,
Jane Park
Head of Platform Partnerships
Medicore Health

Attachment: Medicore_RFP_Q3.pdf (1.2MB)
From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: Jane Park <jane.park@medicore.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 11:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Medicore VPC: initial ask + budget guardrails

Hi Jane — appreciated the clear RFP. High level response below; I'll follow up with a short slide and a pricing matrix.

Summary options (initial proposal):
1) Licensing split
   - Perpetual site license: one-time invoice per site (license key + entitlement).
   - Platform fee: annual, covers control-plane, dashboarding, telemetry, and KV cache management. Can be invoiced annually or amortized monthly.

2) Pilot concession
   - Pilot term (90 days): 50% platform-fee discount for first 90 days OR full platform-fee credit equal to month 1 if pilot converts to production within 60 days.

3) SRE / on-call
   - Option A: 24x7 SRE retainer — flat monthly retainer scaled to expected token throughput.
   - Option B: Per-incident pricing + 8x5 business-hours support included.

4) Milestone credits and conversion
   - We can offer a staged credit: 25% of the first-year platform fee credited if pilot converts within 60 days; additional 10% credit if conversion includes a 3-year committed GPU-hour minimum.

Considerations and risks:
- Deep discounts on platform fee create precedent; recommend structuring as timebound credits tied to explicit conversion milestones.
- On-prem topology with multi-site lift may change license footprint.

Next steps I propose:
- I'll attach a two‑tab matrix: pricing bands + pilot-credit scenarios.
- Marissa / David — can you review the credit caps we can approve without escalate to RevOps/legal?

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachment: privdeploy-pricing-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, Jane Park <jane.park@medicore.com>
Cc: david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 13:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Medicore VPC: initial ask + budget guardrails

Thanks Jane — and thanks Soojin for the quick turnaround. Internal notes / negotiation posture below (kept on-thread so Medicore sees our transparency):

High-level negotiation posture we can present as an initial offer:
- License: standard one-time site license at list with 10% onboarding discount if signed within 30 days.
- Platform fee: annualized, but offer ability to amortize across invoices. Recommend baseline platform fee with two options: (A) 12-month annual fee, (B) 12-month fee with 50% first-90-days concession (credit).
- Pilot credit structure (preferred):
   * If pilot converts within 60 days: credit 30% of month 1 platform fee (applied to first invoice after conversion).
   * If conversion includes 3-year commit: incremental 15% credit on year-1 platform fee (stacking on pilot credit up to cap).
- SRE: offer a 6-month discounted retainer for pilot (40% off) that transitions to full retainer on production, or per-incident at $X/hour with a monthly cap.

SLA tempo (response windows we should propose):
- Pilot: P3 (4 business hours), P2 (8 business hours), P1 (next-business-hour escalation to engineering).
- Production: P3 (2 business hours), P2 (4 business hours), P1 (1 hour, with guaranteed on-call handoff).

Limits and guardrails we need to include in the commercial summary:
- Credit caps: total credits cannot exceed 40% of year-1 platform fee unless approved by revenue leadership (DEAL-5498).
- Platform fee amortization is allowed but not convertible to cash refunds.
- Legal: request a standard IP/escrow clause; we will not accept unrestricted source escrow without enterprise contract.

David — please confirm maximum credit authority we can offer (per deal) and any additional redlines legal will require for pilot->prod conversion clauses. Jane — we're happy to formalize this into a one‑pager + a redline-friendly term sheet.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head, Customer Solutions

Soojin / Marissa — this is very helpful, thank you. A couple quick items and next steps: 

1) Please send the single-slide commercial summary + the pricing matrix by COB tomorrow so our procurement can prepare an internal ask.
2) For the pilot credit, Medicore prefers a simple: "convert within 60 days -> 30% credit to month-1 platform fee" (we can discuss stacking later).
3) We will not sign any escrow that includes full-source access; the procurement team asks for a standard escrow with a limited-use clause.
4) Meeting: can we do a 30-minute call on Thursday 10AM PT to review the single slide and a high-level SOW outline?

If you can also include the DocuSign-ready term-sheet link, that will speed things up. Looking forward to the slide.

Thanks,
Jane
Head of Platform Partnerships
Medicore Health
